## Description

Euler's method is the simplest one-step numerical solver for an initial value problem
$y' = f(t,y)$, $y(t_0)=y_0$. It advances the solution by following the local tangent
at each grid point:

$$
y_{n+1} = y_n + h\,f(t_n,y_n), \qquad t_{n+1}=t_n+h.
$$

For smooth problems, Euler has local truncation error $O(h^2)$ and global error
$O(h)$, so reducing the step size improves accuracy linearly. The modified Euler
(Heun) predictor-corrector method averages endpoint slopes and improves global
accuracy to $O(h^2)$.

## Animations

Each animation below shows the **numerical solution trace** for the IVP
$y' = 1 - t\sqrt[3]{y}$, $y(0)=1$ on $0 \le t \le 5$, computed with $n=200$ steps
($h=0.025$). Each frame adds five steps (0.125 in $t$); the connecting curve passes
through every computed point.
The dashed black curve is a high-accuracy reference trajectory computed with fixed-step
RK4 at $h=10^{-4}$ and shown for direct visual error comparison.

Legacy archive note: the original `Euleraa.gif` and `MEuleraa.gif` files were missing
from the recovered animation folders, so these are reconstructed from the module's
worked-example equations and parameters (Examples 11-12).

### Case 1 - Forward Euler, $y' = 1 - t\sqrt[3]{y}$, $y(0)=1$, $0 \le t \le 5$, $n=200$ steps ($h=0.025$)

**Behavior:** Forward Euler runs above the dashed RK4 reference until $t=2.9$, by at
most $0.017$ near $t=1.7$; after that it lies just below, by less than $0.002$, and
ends at $y(5)\approx0.0081186$ against the exact $0.0081199$. For steps longer than
about $h=0.0485$, $h\,|\partial f/\partial y|$ exceeds Euler's stability limit 2 before
$t=5$ (because $\partial f/\partial y=-t/(3y^{2/3})$ reaches $-41.3$ at $t=5$), and from
then on errors are amplified instead of damped; just above $h=0.0485$ this affects only
the last steps, but at the legacy module's $h=0.125$ ($n=40$) it starts at $t\approx3.68$
and the computed values zig-zag after $t=4.25$, jump to $0.232$ at $t=4.875$ and end at
$y(5)\approx-0.0174$, although the exact solution stays positive.

[Julia source](eulersmethodaa.jl)

![Forward Euler animation with step h = 0.025 (n = 200) for y' = 1 - t cbrt(y), y(0)=1 over 0 <= t <= 5: the magenta trace builds five steps per frame, runs slightly above the dashed RK4 reference over the hump (peak about 1.46 near t = 0.9) and then follows it down to y ≈ 0.0081 at t = 5](eulersmethodaa.gif)

### Case 2 - Modified Euler (Heun), same IVP and grid

**Behavior:** Averaging the slopes at both ends of each step keeps Heun within
$1.8\times10^{-4}$ of the dashed RK4 reference, against $0.017$ for forward Euler on the
same grid, and it ends at $y(5)\approx0.0081213$. Heun has the same stability limit as
Euler, $h\,|\partial f/\partial y|<2$, so at $h=0.125$ ($n=40$) errors are amplified
instead of damped from $t\approx3.68$: it stays within $0.0071$ of the reference up to
$t=3.875$, then its values turn upward and end at $y(5)\approx0.251$, about 31 times the
exact value.

[Julia source](eulersmethodbb.jl)

![Modified Euler (Heun) animation with step h = 0.025 (n = 200) for y' = 1 - t cbrt(y), y(0)=1 over 0 <= t <= 5: the magenta trace builds five steps per frame and lies on the dashed RK4 reference throughout, rising to about 1.45 near t = 0.9 and falling to y ≈ 0.0081 at t = 5](eulersmethodbb.gif)
